subject: Inference surface inventory and lateral risk matrix - RFP packet
messages:
From: Timothy Hale <timothy.hale@peregrinefinancial.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com; ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@peregrinefinancial.com; security+rfp@peregrinefinancial.com
Date: 2028-12-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: RFP - inventory & lateral risk matrix request

Hi Grace / Ben,

Thanks for the call earlier. As part of our security evaluation for the upcoming RFP, we need a concise inventory of the "inference surface" for Redwood's hosted and dedicated deployments, plus a lateral risk matrix that maps potential attacker movement between components. Key asks:

- A flattened inventory (services/processes/endpoints) and which lanes (control plane, data plane, sidecars, kv cache, metrics) they belong to.
- Where tenant boundaries are enforced and how (network ACLs, microsegmentation, sidecar isolation).
- Typical attack paths and mitigations, prioritized by likelihood/impact.
- Any residual risks that require compensating controls.

Can you provide a short packet (slide + CSV) and a one‑page threat narrative focused on lateral movement? We're on a 2-week review cadence so a first pass by 12/11 would be ideal.

Thanks,
Tim
Director, Infrastructure Security
Peregrine Financial
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Timothy Hale <timothy.hale@peregrinefinancial.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com; marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-12-08T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP - inventory & lateral risk matrix request

Tim —

Appreciate the clear asks. Ben and Marissa and I will assemble:

1) an "inference surface inventory" workbook (tabbed by component and traffic direction),
2) a CSV lateral-risk matrix mapping entry vector -> lateral target -> controls -> residual risk score,
3) a short 1-page threat narrative describing plausible attacker progressions and mitigations.

We have a recent topology diagram (network_topology_v3.png) and an inventory spreadsheet we'll adapt. We'll include explicit markers for: public ingress, load balancers, model serving pods, KV cache hosts, sidecar proxies, control-plane APIs, metrics/telemetry collectors, and customer-managed VPC peering endpoints.

Delivering first draft by 2028-12-11 EOD PST. Is that acceptable? Also, any format preferences for the risk matrix scoring (1-5, qualitative)?

Cheers,
Grace
Head of Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Timothy Hale <timothy.hale@peregrinefinancial.com>

On 2028-12-08 11:04, grace_oconnor@redwood.com wrote:
> Delivering first draft by 2028-12-11 EOD PST. Is that acceptable? Also, any format preferences for the risk matrix scoring (1-5, qualitative)?

That timeline works. Use a 1-5 numeric scoring for both likelihood and impact and include a short justification column. If you can include quick answers to three specific questions in the packet, that would be helpful:

Q1) Under what conditions could a tenant request reach another tenant's KV cache?
Q2) How is the control plane authenticated/authorized from operator tooling versus customer-managed network peers?
Q3) What are detection hooks/telemetry available to detect lateral movement inside a node/pod?

Thanks — looking forward to your draft.

Tim
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Timothy Hale <timothy.hale@peregrinefinancial.com>; grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com; jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2028-12-09T08:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP - inventory & lateral risk matrix request

Tim / team —

Attached are the initial artifacts: inference-surface-inventory.xlsx (tabbed), network_topology_v3.png, and a CSV lateral-risk-matrix.csv. Summary highlights below:

- Tenant boundaries: enforced primarily via namespace-level network policies + host-level iptables on serving hosts for hosted and dedicated variants; for Private deployments we provide a packaged operator configuration that integrates with customer VPC ACLs.
- KV cache: per-tenant cache shards; routing enforced by the serving runtime's tenant-id header and sidecar ACLs. A misrouted request requires compromised sidecar credentials or operator-level control-plane access.
- Control plane auth: mutual TLS between operator tooling and the control plane, backed by short-lived certs from our internal CA. Customer-managed peers (VPC peering) require static allowlists and TLS with customer-provided cert bundles.
- Detection hooks: token-level tracing, live request sampling, per-pod connection graphs exported to our telemetry pipeline; IDS-style anomalous egress alerts are available as an add-on.

Please review the CSV for the scoring and the short narrative (sheet "ThreatNarrative"). We'll iterate on any gaps.

Attachments: inference-surface-inventory.xlsx (xlsx, 210 KB); network_topology_v3.png (png, 480 KB); lateral-risk-matrix.csv (csv, 34 KB)

-ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Timothy Hale <timothy.hale@peregrinefinancial.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com; grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@peregrinefinancial.com; security+rfp@peregrinefinancial.com
Date: 2028-12-11T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP - inventory & lateral risk matrix request

Thanks, Ben — received and reviewed. Quick feedback after an internal sync:

- The KV cache separation looks solid; please add a short note on key rotation cadence and what happens to stale cache shards when a tenant is deprovisioned.
- For control plane auth, include an example of the mutual TLS certificate lifecycle (rotation interval, revocation process).
- On detection: the sampling windows and retention for request traces matter to us — can you state typical retention and whether traces are tenant-scoped?

If you can add those clarifications in an updated one-page appendix, we can close this item for the security review. Can you target 2028-12-13 for a final appendix?

Regards,
Tim
Director, Infrastructure Security
Peregrine Financial
